ns2:section.sectionText: SP25 - ENGL 524 - Seminar in Early Modern Literature - Re-reading Embodiment in Early Modern Britain, 1570-1670- Lori Newcomb - Early modern Britain conceived its categories of human embodiment, including gender, nationality, race, rank, and religion, as deeply intertwined yet surprisingly fluid. Contemporary scholarship in critical bibliography, critical race studies, and queer and trans* studies, is now exposing both fluidity and hardening, particularly as whiteness became the category of embodied difference most forcefully associated with Englishness. To trace this process, we’ll read drama, poetry, and prose by male and female authors, along with samples of conduct books, travel accounts, and street literature. Secondary readings will include generative scholarship by Kim F. Hall, Ania Loomba, Imtiaz Habib, and Valerie Traub, along with very recent work by Brandi Adams, Bernadette Andrea, Patricia Akhimie, David Sterling Brown, Matthieu Chapman, Noémie Ndiaye, and Melissa Sanchez, among others. A particular focus of the seminar will be the ambivalent role of printed books in disseminating constructions of embodiment to British readerships. Course projects will include interpretive work on the materiality of primary texts, tapping the magnificent collections of our Rare Book and Manuscript Library.
